title: Past Modals — Odd One Out
instructions: Read the situation. Three of the four sentences use a past modal in a way that logically fits it. One doesn't belong — tap it to knock it out.

rounds.situation: Why did Alison fail her driving test?

options.text: She <<must have>> been nervous.
She <<can't have>> been focused.
She <<might have>> used her phone while driving.
She <<ought to have>> tried again.

rounds.explain: 'Ought to have' gives advice about what to do next — it doesn't explain why she failed.

rounds.situation: The lights in the office are still on but everyone left hours ago.

options.text: Someone <<must have>> forgotten to switch them off.
They <<can't have>> been left on purpose.
The cleaner <<might>> still be working late.
They <<should have>> turned them off by now.

rounds.explain: 'Should have' is a criticism of what didn't happen, not a guess about why it happened.

rounds.situation: Tom arrived at the party two hours late and didn't apologise.

options.text: He <<might have>> got stuck in traffic.
He <<can't have>> known what time it started.
He <<must have>> lost track of time.
He <<needn't have>> come at all.

rounds.explain: 'Needn't have' comments on an unnecessary action — it doesn't explain why he was late.

rounds.situation: The plants in the garden have all died, even though it rained every day.

options.text: They <<must have>> been overwatered.
Someone <<could have>> used the wrong fertiliser.
They <<can't have>> got enough sunlight.
We <<ought to have>> watered them more.

rounds.explain: 'Ought to have' is advice about the past — and it contradicts the situation, since it rained every day.

rounds.situation: Maria's essay scored much higher than everyone else's.

options.text: She <<must have>> worked really hard on it.
She <<might have>> got help from a tutor.
She <<can't have>> written it in one evening.
She <<shouldn't have>> submitted it so early.

rounds.explain: 'Shouldn't have' criticises a different choice — it doesn't explain the high score.

rounds.situation: When the police arrived, the shop's back door was wide open and the till was empty.

options.text: The thief <<must have>> got in through the back.
It <<can't have>> been an inside job — the door was forced.
The alarm <<might have>> failed to go off.
The owner <<should have>> called the police earlier.

rounds.explain: That's a criticism of the owner, not a deduction about how the burglary happened.

options.text: He <<might not have>> slept well.
He <<must have>> stayed up late working.
He <<can't have>> gone to bed before midnight.
He <<ought to>> go to bed earlier tonight.

rounds.explain: That's advice for tonight, not a guess about why he looks tired now.

rounds.situation: The cake collapsed in the middle as soon as it came out of the oven.

options.text: The oven temperature <<must have>> been too low.
Someone <<could have>> opened the door too early.
The mixture <<can't have>> had enough flour.
You <<needn't have>> added so much sugar.

rounds.explain: 'Needn't have' is a comment about an unnecessary step — it doesn't explain why the cake collapsed.

rounds.situation: Jake passed the exam despite never attending a single class.

options.text: He <<must have>> studied on his own.
He <<might have>> copied someone else's notes.
The exam <<can't have>> been very difficult.
He <<should have>> gone to more classes.

rounds.explain: That's criticism about attendance — it doesn't explain how he managed to pass.

rounds.situation: The dog started barking loudly at 3 a.m.

options.text: It <<must have>> heard something outside.
Someone <<might have>> been walking past the house.
It <<can't have>> been dreaming — it was standing by the door.
We <<ought to have>> trained it better.

rounds.explain: That's general advice about training — it doesn't explain the barking that night.

rounds.situation: All the photographs from the trip came out blurry.

options.text: The camera <<must have>> been faulty.
Someone <<could have>> moved the camera while taking the shot.
It <<can't have>> been very sunny that day.
You <<should have>> bought a better camera.

rounds.explain: That's a criticism of a past decision, not an explanation for the blurriness itself.

rounds.situation: Sophie looked completely shocked when she opened the door and saw her friends there.

options.text: She <<can't have>> known about the surprise party.
She <<might have>> forgotten it was her birthday.
Someone <<must have>> kept the secret well.
She <<needn't have>> been so surprised.

rounds.explain: That's a comment saying the reaction wasn't necessary — it doesn't explain why she was surprised.
